summary: Settlement processing on settlement-service is stalled because order-service deployment dep-6010 (v2.16.0, live 2026-05-12T07:40:00Z) renamed the OrderExecuted field 'qty'->'quantity' and stamped the event header 'v2', while the settlement-service consumer still expects schema v1; the resulting message at orders-3@8841207 cannot be deserialized and becomes a poison message that blocks partition orders-3 and is retried tens of thousands of times, so consumption collapses (~62 -> ~0.4 req/s) and consumer lag climbs monotonically to 60k+. The conclusion is supported by verified, content-specific evidence (exact schema-vocabulary match between the deploy's declared changes and the consumer's error, tight temporal ordering, fixed-offset poison retry, stall-shaped resource profile) with confidence 0.72 (medium, capped) because the producer->partition hop is circumstantial. H2 (cfg-3004 poll settings), H3 (broker/DB event), H4 (volume burst) and H5 (metrics artifact) are each contradicted by verified observations, not merely dismissed, though a silent unrecorded broker/DB event can only be weakened, not positively excluded. The one open sub-question - producer shipped uncoordinated v2 vs. consumer is stale v1 - names the same origin and the same causal chain, so it does not change the ranking or the fix direction.

ranked_hypotheses.title: order-service v2 OrderExecuted schema (qty→quantity, v2 header) produced a record the v1 settlement consumer cannot deserialize
ranked_hypotheses.statement: dep-6010 (order-service v2.16.0, live at 07:40:00Z, the only deployment in the fleet window) renamed the OrderExecuted field 'qty'→'quantity' and stamped the event schema version header 'v2'. settlement-service's consumer still expects schema v1 and requires field 'qty'; on orders-3@8841207 it fails deserialization ('missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)'), the record becomes a poison message, the retry loop re-attempts the same offset tens of thousands of times ('partition blocked'), the consumer never commits past it, so consumption collapses to a ~0.4 req/s floor and lag grows monotonically to 60k+. The fault ORIGIN is the uncoordinated OrderExecuted v2 schema change introduced by dep-6010; the two readings of the same origin are (i) the producer shipped a schema change without the consumer being upgraded — fix = revert/coordinate the producer, or (ii) the consumer is stale (v1) relative to an intended v2 rollout — fix = upgrade the settlement consumer. Both readings share the same origin and the same causal chain and are therefore ONE hypothesis; the open detail is which side is 'at fault' and the producer's exact identity.

causal_chain.claim: order-service deploys v2.16.0 at 07:40:00Z, renaming OrderExecuted 'qty'→'quantity' and adding event schema version header v2; it is the only deployment anywhere in 06:00-09:59 and the only order-service change in the whole 2026-05-11→05-12 window
order-service's sole event-emission channel is queue-produce to kafka ('orders'), so any v2 OrderExecuted it emits must traverse that single producer edge
~2 min later settlement-service hits a deserialize failure on orders-3@8841207 with exactly matching vocabulary: missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)
The undeserializable record is treated as a poison message and retried against the same fixed offset tens of thousands of times, blocking partition orders-3
Because the partition cannot advance, consumption collapses to a ~0.4 req/s floor while CPU stays ~70% busy-spinning on retries and HTTP 5xx stays flat
Lag inflects at the 07:40 bucket and climbs every bucket thereafter to 60k+, matching 'no settlements posted'

assumptions: The v2 OrderExecuted record at orders-3 offset 8841207 was produced by order-service — no producer-side publish log nor topic→partition mapping is retrievable (F24, F36, F40), so the link rests on 2-min timestamp adjacency plus exact schema-vocabulary match
order-service and settlement-service meet on the same topic 'orders' / partition orders-3 (graph edges carry no topic or partition names, F4/F20)

No other producer's v2 change could have emitted the offending record — payment-service is the only other producer on kafka and has 0 deployments in the window (F22), but nobody verified payment-service does not emit an OrderExecuted-style v2 payload
The producer/consumer v1→v2 rollout was not coordinated (no consumer upgrade accompanies dep-6010), leaving a mixed-version window — this is an inference, not an observed fact
The stall is confined to partition orders-3; group-level consumer_lag is not partition-split (F30, F32, F33, F35), so broader partition impact is unverified

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared dependency (kafka broker partition reassignment or ledger-db write stall) froze the consumer
ranked_hypotheses.statement: settlement-service's only two dependencies are the shared kafka broker and the shared ledger-db. A broker-side partition reassignment/maintenance or DB write saturation could block the consumer's queue-consume or db path, stalling settlements and growing lag — mirroring HIST-112/HIST-104 (consumer lost partition assignment during broker maintenance). No change event documents such an action, and the observed failure signature (poison-message schema mismatch on a fixed offset) is not the signature this cause would produce.

causal_chain.claim: kafka and ledger-db are shared components reachable from settlement-service, so third parties can affect it
Broker maintenance / partition reassignment is assumed to have occurred, revoking partition assignment or rebalancing the consumer group
Consumer stops advancing offsets; request_rate collapses ~07:45 and lag climbs to 60k+

assumptions: An undocumented broker or DB event occurred (change tools record no kafka/ledger-db change in the window)
A rebalance would land in the same 07:40-07:42 bucket as the order-service deploy
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The observable failure is a partition-blocked poison-message retry on a single schema-mismatched offset (F8, F7), not a lost-assignment/rebalance pattern: zero 'rebalance'/'assigned' log matches on settlement-service in-window (F28). No kafka or ledger-db change or event is recorded in 06:00-09:59 (F17, F3, F25), and CPU pinned ~70% with request_rate ~0.4 while memory is flat fits a deserialization/retry busy-loop, not broker or DB saturation (F11). HIST-112/104 are past-incident leads explicitly not evidence and their signatures (no schema mismatch) do not match (F19). Exclusion rests on absence of recorded events plus missing broker/DB telemetry (no per-partition produce metric, kafka consumer_lag not_found), so a silent broker/DB event is weakened but not positively disproven — hence kept as the leading residual alternative, not zeroed.

ranked_hypotheses.title: settlement-service consumer poll-settings change (cfg-3004) starved the poll loop / caused a rebalance or offset stall
ranked_hypotheses.statement: cfg-3004 reduced consumer.max.poll.records from 500 to 200 on settlement-service at 07:35:00Z — the reporter's suspicion. Smaller poll batches throttled throughput and/or the config reload triggered a consumer-group rebalance or an invalid poll configuration that stalled the consumer, so lag grew even though the consumer was nominally healthy.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-3004 reduces consumer.max.poll.records 500→200 on settlement-service at 07:35:00Z (only config change in the window; no rollback)
Smaller poll batches could reduce per-poll throughput and slow settlement writes as intended
config reload on the consumer group is assumed to have triggered a rebalance/stall that froze offset commits
Result: consumption floor ~0.4 req/s and monotonic lag growth from ~07:40

assumptions: The config reload caused a rebalance or blocked polling (no consumer-group state or rebalance event was retrieved; log search for 'rebalance'/'assigned' returned 0)
A poll-size reduction alone can hold throughput at ~0.4 req/s with CPU pinned at ~70%
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The verified failure is content-specific, not rate-specific: 'missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)' on a single fixed offset plus a poison-message retry loop ('retrying orders-3@8841207, partition blocked', attempt 92490) starting 07:42:14Z — 7 min 14 s after cfg-3004 and 2 min after dep-6010, so the stall tracks message CONTENT, not batch size. Reducing max.poll.records 500→200 leaves 200 records per poll and cannot produce per-message deserialize failures, a blocked partition, or a ~0.4 req/s floor (F16). cfg-3004 remains at most an aggravating factor, never the origin. No rebalance/assignment log text exists on settlement-service in 07:35-09:59 (F28).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Upstream trade-volume burst or replay/backfill overflowed the orders queue without a code/config fault
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A burst of trade volume or a replay/backfill from an upstream producer (trade-service / clearing feed) flooded the 'orders' topic, so lag grew despite unchanged consumer throughput. Consumer lag grows purely because arrival rate exceeds service rate.

causal_chain.claim: Upstream producer emits a large burst/replay of OrderExecuted events into the orders topic
Arrival rate exceeds settlement-service consumption rate, so lag climbs
Lag reaches 60k+ and settlements appear stuck

assumptions: A volume burst occurred (no producer throughput metrics, topic messaging metrics, or producer-side telemetry were retrieved)
An upstream volume surge could exist without any deployment or config change (only dep-6010 and cfg-3004 exist in the window)
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: A volume surge degrades throughput gradually; the evidence shows a near-total halt — request_rate collapses from ~62 to ~0.4 req/s (F10) with CPU pinned ~70% (F11) and no HTTP 5xx (F12), a blocked consumer rather than an overloaded one. A burst also cannot produce a per-message schema deserialize error or a fixed-offset poison-message retry loop (F7, F8). No producer throughput or topic-arrival metric exists, so normal traffic at onset is unproven, but nothing in the change data shows a replay/backfill trigger either.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Reporting/metrics artifact: settlements are actually progressing and consumer_lag is a stale or mis-scoped metric
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The apparent stall is an instrumentation artifact — the settlement workload may be partially completing while the group-level consumer_lag series (which has no partition dimension and is downsampled to 18-minute buckets) misrepresents progress, or lag is measuring a deprecated/stale topic. This would explain 'zero settlements processed' as a reporting gap rather than a true processing halt.

causal_chain.claim: consumer_lag is a group-level aggregate exposed only at coarse 18-minute buckets and there is no per-partition lag or processed-settlement metric, so metric interpretation is fragile
If lag is stale/mis-scoped, the 'no settlements posted' report reflects broken instrumentation rather than a real stall
Apparent symptom: lag 60k+ and zero settlements

assumptions: The metric could be stale despite a clean monotonic climb from a stable baseline
Error logs and collapsed request_rate could coexist with real progress
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: A pure instrumentation artifact cannot produce the corroborated partition-blocked poison-message retry at a fixed offset (F8, F27) nor the near-total collapse of request_rate from ~62 to ~0.4 req/s (F10). The metric objection is real but limited (no partition dimension, coarse buckets), and it does not explain the error logs — it is a metrics-quality caveat, not the origin.

facts.statement: dep-6010 (order-service v2.16.0) went live at 2026-05-12T07:40:00Z and is the only deployment anywhere in the fleet in 06:00-09:59Z; its declared changes are 'OrderExecuted event: rename field qty -> quantity', 'add field venue', 'event schema version header v2', status live, rolled_back_at null.

The first settlement-service ERROR appears at 2026-05-12T07:42:14Z with the signature 'failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)' - the deploy's declared schema vocabulary matches the consumer error verbatim.

All 409 matched ERROR logs in settlement-service fall into exactly two patterns - schema mismatch (213x) and poison-message retry (196x) - 100% bound to partition orders-3 at offset 8841207, spanning 07:42:14Z-09:58:31Z.

The consumer is stuck re-attempting the same offset and never advances past it: 'poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt 92490), partition blocked' appears from 07:44:51Z with attempt counters in the tens of thousands.

Consumer lag inflects at the 07:40 bucket: baseline 06:30-07:35 stays in the 35-64 range, then jumps to avg 515.03 / max 1306.47 at 07:40:00Z and climbs every bucket to avg ~60220 / max 61605 at ~09:55Z.
Consumption effectively ceased, not merely slowed: request_rate collapses from a steady ~62 req/s through 07:35 to avg 0.41 at 07:45:00Z and stays flat at ~0.40 req/s for the rest of the window.

Resource profile is stall-like rather than saturation: cpu_pct rises from ~28% baseline to ~70% from 07:42:00Z onward while request_rate is ~0.4 req/s, and memory_pct stays flat at ~49-51% with no growth or OOM trend.

HTTP error_rate stays flat at ~0.2% across the entire window including onset, i.e. the failure is not surfacing as HTTP 5xx - consistent with a consumer-side blocking stall rather than request-serving failure.

The only config change anywhere in 06:00-09:59Z is cfg-3004 on settlement-service: 'consumer.max.poll.records' reduced 500 -> 200 at 2026-05-12T07:35:00Z, with no rollback recorded; it changes only batch size, not deserialization/schema handling, and precedes onset by 7m14s.
No rebalance or partition-assignment log text exists on settlement-service in 07:35-09:59Z: 'rebalance' -> 0 matches and 'assigned' -> 0 matches.

settlement-service's dependency graph has only two edges - queue-consume to kafka and db to ledger-db - both shared components, and no deployment or config change is recorded for kafka, ledger-db or any other platform component in 06:00-09:59Z.

The 'orders' topic (kafka) has exactly four edges: producers order-service and payment-service, consumers settlement-service and notification-service; no other service produces to or consumes from kafka.

payment-service, the other producer on kafka, has 0 deployments in 2026-05-11T00:00Z - 2026-05-12T09:59Z and no matching change record, and shows zero matches for the v2 signature ('missing required field', 'schema v1 expected') over 07:35-09:59Z.

order-service records exactly 0 config changes in the window and only one deployment (dep-6010), and its sole event-emission channel is the single 'order-service -> kafka queue-produce' edge; kafka is its only publish path.

No producer-side record exists for the offending message: order-service logs contain zero publish/produce records and zero lines mentioning 'OrderExecuted', 'orders-3', 'qty' or '8841207' at INFO+ over 04:00-09:59Z, and no producer/partition/offset metric exists on order-service or kafka.

No producer->topic-partition mapping or producer config is retrievable for dep-6010/order-service; the deployment record carries no topic or partition fields, so the specific partition that OrderExecuted v2 is written to is not documented.

Neither settlement-service nor the kafka component exposes a partition-dimensioned lag/commit metric: settlement-service available_metrics are only [consumer_lag, cpu_pct, db_pool_in_use, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts] ('consumer_lag_partition' -> not_found), and kafka offers only [cpu_pct, messages_in_per_s, under_replicated_partitions].

Historical precedents HIST-112 and HIST-104 match the lag/stuck symptom but are broker partition-assignment/rebalance events and do not match the current poison-message/schema-mismatch signature; they are leads, not evidence about this incident.

notification-service shows no deserialize failures in 07:30-09:59Z ('deserialize' at WARN+ -> 0 matches), and ledger-db, portfolio-service and market-data-service each show 0 matches for 'missing required field' over 07:35-09:59Z in fully covered data ranges.

assumptions: The v2 OrderExecuted record at orders-3 offset 8841207 was produced by order-service: no producer-side publish log, produce metric, or topic->partition mapping is retrievable, so this load-bearing hop rests on 2-minute timestamp adjacency plus exact schema-vocabulary match (F24, F36, F38, F40).

order-service and settlement-service meet on the same topic 'orders' / partition orders-3: dependency-graph edges carry no topic or partition names, so the shared topic is inferred, not observed (F4, F20).

No other producer could have emitted the offending record: payment-service is the only other producer on kafka and has 0 deployments and 0 matches for the v2 signature in the window (F22, F41), but it was not positively verified that payment-service cannot emit an OrderExecuted-style v2 payload.

The order-service producer rollout of OrderExecuted v2 and the settlement-service v1 consumer were not coordinated, leaving a mixed-version window: this is an inference from the change data, not an observed fact (F2, F14).
The stall is confined to partition orders-3: lag telemetry is group-level only with no partition dimension (F30, F32, F33, F35), so broader per-partition impact is unverified.

Settlement is genuinely not progressing rather than appearing so: no 'processed_settlements' metric exists and the conclusion leans on the collapsed request_rate (~0.4 req/s) plus corroborated error logs (F10, F26).

A silent, unrecorded broker-side or DB-side event in 07:40-07:45Z is not positively excluded: no kafka/ledger-db telemetry exists at all, and absence of a recorded change event does not prove absence of an event (F3, F17, F25).

The remaining open sub-question - producer shipped uncoordinated v2 vs. settlement consumer is stale v1 - does not change the origin, the causal chain, or the ranking; both readings are addressed by reverting/coordinating dep-6010 or upgrading the consumer.

(demoted from facts: no verified observation backs it) A poll-batch-size change cannot produce a per-message deserialize failure, a blocked single partition, or a sustained ~0.4 req/s floor; the observed failure is tied to message CONTENT on a fixed offset, not to poll batch size.

timeline.event: Config change cfg-3004 on settlement-service: consumer.max.poll.records reduced 500 -> 200 by m.das ('Smaller poll batches to smooth DB writes'). No rollback recorded; the only config change in the window.

dep-6010 order-service v2.16.0 goes live (author a.khan, 'Order events v2'): 'OrderExecuted event: rename field qty -> quantity', 'add field venue', 'event schema version header v2'. The only deployment in the fleet window; status live, not rolled back.
Consumer lag inflects at the same bucket: baseline 35-64 (06:30-07:35) jumps to avg 515.03 / max 1306.47, then climbs monotonically to ~60k+ through 09:55Z.
order-service logs only its rollout marker: 'deployment dep-6010 (v2.16.0) rollout complete, all pods ready' - no publish or produce record.
First settlement-service ERROR: 'failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)' - 2m14s after dep-6010.
Resource profile shifts to stall-like: cpu_pct rises from ~28% baseline to ~70% and stays there while memory_pct remains flat ~49-51%; HTTP error_rate stays flat at ~0.2%.
Poison-message retry loop begins: 'poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt 92490), partition blocked' - the consumer is stuck on the same offset.
Consumption effectively ceases: request_rate collapses from ~62 req/s to ~0.41 req/s and stays flat at ~0.40 for the rest of the window.
Incident INC-010 reported by on-call SRE: no settlements posted ~40 minutes, settlement consumer lag 60k and climbing, zero settlements processed.
Last matched ERROR of the same two patterns (schema mismatch / poison-message retry) on orders-3; lag has climbed to ~60k+ with zero recovery.

recommended_actions.action: Mitigate on the producer side: revert or coordinate dep-6010 (order-service v2.16.0, live 2026-05-12T07:40:00Z) so OrderExecuted is again emitted with the v1-compatible 'qty' field (or add v1-compatible emission alongside v2) until the settlement consumer is upgraded. This is the only change in the window and the reversible direction.
recommended_actions.rationale: dep-6010 is the only deployment in the fleet window and its declared change vocabulary ('rename qty -> quantity', 'v2 header') matches the consumer error verbatim; reverting/coordinating it restores a schema the v1 consumer can deserialize and clears the blocking condition at its origin.

recommended_actions.action: In parallel, unblock partition orders-3 by patching the settlement-service consumer's poison-message handling to skip-and-quarantine the failed offset (send orders-3@8841207 to a DLQ and commit past it) rather than retrying it indefinitely.
recommended_actions.rationale: The consumer is stuck re-attempting the same fixed offset tens of thousands of times ('partition blocked', attempt 92490), which is what pins throughput at ~0.4 req/s and drives monotonic lag growth; skipping the single poison offset restores consumption immediately and is safe under either reading of the producer/consumer fault.

recommended_actions.action: Verify recovery: confirm settlement-service request_rate returns to its ~62 req/s baseline, partition orders-3 advances past offset 8841207 with new offsets committed, consumer lag declines monotonically from the ~60k peak, and CPU returns from ~70% toward the ~28% baseline.
recommended_actions.rationale: These are the verified pre-incident and stall-state signatures; their reversal is the direct evidence that the poison-message block is cleared rather than merely relocating.

recommended_actions.action: Complete the schema rollout properly: upgrade the settlement-service OrderExecuted consumer to schema v2 (accept 'quantity' and the 'venue' field, tolerate v1 during transition) so producer and consumer are back in lockstep, then re-enable the earlier cfg-3004 poll setting or re-tune it deliberately.
recommended_actions.rationale: The failure is a version skew between the dep-6010 v2 producer and a v1 consumer; upgrading the consumer resolves the mismatch at its origin and removes the mixed-version window. cfg-3004 was verified not to be the cause (batch-size change cannot produce a per-message deserialize failure) but should not be left as an unvalidated change.

recommended_actions.action: Add and enforce producer/consumer schema-contract compatibility gating in CI/CD: block a deployment that changes an event schema version (e.g. dep-6010's v2 header) unless registered consumers are verified compatible or upgraded, and require consumer-group compatibility checks as a pre-deploy gate.
recommended_actions.rationale: The origin is an uncoordinated OrderExecuted v1->v2 schema change shipped by a lone deployment with no accompanying consumer upgrade; preventing that class of change prevents recurrence.

recommended_actions.action: Instrument the gap that made this hard to close: add a partition-dimensioned consumer lag/commit metric to settlement-service and per-partition produce/offset visibility on order-service/kafka, plus producer-side publish logging (which currently records nothing at INFO+).
recommended_actions.rationale: No producer->partition mapping, per-partition lag, or produce metric exists today, which is exactly why the producer->orders-3@8841207 hop and the partition-blast radius remain circumstantial; closing these gaps makes future schema/poison-message incidents conclusive rather than correlation-based.

recommended_actions.action: Add alerting on settlement-service consumer lag slope and on poison-message retry attempt counters (e.g. page when a single offset is retried more than N times), instead of relying on a ~40-minute human-detected stall.
recommended_actions.rationale: The poison-message loop ran from 07:44:51Z to 09:58:31Z with lag climbing 35 -> 60k+ before being reported at 08:22Z; an offset-retry or lag-slope alert would catch this in seconds rather than tens of minutes.

data_gaps: Producer identity for the offending record is not observed: no producer-side publish log, produce metric, or order-service->topic-partition mapping exists in the tooling, so 'order-service produced orders-3@8841207' rests on 2-minute adjacency plus exact schema-vocabulary match (F24, F36, F38, F40).

No partition-dimensioned lag/commit series exists for the settlement consumer group or kafka, so whether lag growth is confined to orders-3 or spread across all assigned partitions cannot be determined; only log-embedded partition tags (orders-3@8841207) are available (F32, F34, F35).

No kafka or ledger-db telemetry or change events exist for this window, so a silent, unrecorded broker partition reassignment or ledger-db write stall (the HIST-112/HIST-104 class) cannot be positively excluded - only shown to be unrecorded (F3, F17, F25).

Per-consumer coverage of the v2 deserialize signature is incomplete: only notification-service returned a clean negative (F29) plus ledger-db, portfolio-service and market-data-service for the 'missing required field' variant (F43-F45); 'schema v1 expected'/'header says v2' variants and other potential 'orders' consumers were not all queried before budget exhaustion, so topic-wide blast radius is unverified.
No trade-service or clearing-feed component exists in the platform's known services, so upstream producers named in the incident could not be enumerated or checked for changes near onset.

No GC, disk, or network-pod-level metrics exist for settlement-service, so a GC/serialization-blocking stall cannot be fully differentiated from other blocking causes using resource metrics; the stall-vs-saturation call rests on CPU ~70% with request_rate ~0.4.
The 409 ERROR matches were only partially enumerated (40 returned), so later-window error variants beyond the two dominant patterns may exist but were not inspected.

order-service logging omits event-publish lines entirely (searches for 'OrderExecuted', 'orders-3', 'qty', 'quantity', '8841207' all returned 0 at INFO+), so a producer-side error about the renamed field would not have been visible even if it occurred (F31, F36).
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Producer-side evidence that offset orders-3@8841207 was NOT produced by order-service (e.g. a publish log or produce metric showing order-service's v2 OrderExecuted events routed to a different partition, or another producer identified for that offset) would break H1's origin hop and move the fault elsewhere.

Evidence that another 'orders' consumer (beyond notification-service) also fails to deserialize the same v2 record would indicate a producer-side/shared fault rather than a consumer-specific v1 staleness, changing the fix emphasis (though not the origin).

A recorded or observable kafka broker partition-reassignment/maintenance event or a ledger-db write-stall coincident with 07:40-07:42Z would resurrect H3, since that alternative is only weakened (no broker/DB telemetry exists), not disproven.

Evidence that settlement-service's poison-message retry loop started before dep-6010's 07:40:00Z live time, or that the lag inflection preceded the deploy, would decouple the schema change from onset and break the temporal-ordering argument.
A producer throughput/topic-arrival series showing a genuine volume burst at onset, or per-partition lag showing lag growth on partitions other than orders-3, would re-open H4 (capacity saturation).
A reversal of the request_rate collapse (i.e. consumption continuing at normal rate during the window) would support H5 (metrics artifact) and undercut the poison-message-blocked explanation.
An observed change on kafka or ledger-db in 06:00-09:59Z would invalidate the 'no third-party change' basis for ruling out H3.

findings.statement: Consumer lag inflects at the same minute as the first error: baseline 06:30-07:35 stays in range 35-64 (max 63.97 at 07:25), then jumps to avg 515.03 / max 1306.47 at 07:40:00Z and climbs every 5-min bucket thereafter to avg 60220.76 / max 61605.53 at 09:55:00Z.

Consumption effectively ceased: request_rate collapses from a steady ~62 req/s through 07:35 to avg 0.41 at 07:45:00Z and stays flat at ~0.40 req/s for the rest of the window (last 0.38). This is a near-total halt of processing setup, not a slowdown.

Resource pattern is stall-like, not saturation: cpu_pct jumps from ~28% baseline (07:33 avg 27.26) to ~70% from 07:42:00Z onward (avg 69.34, max 72.4) and stays ~70% (last avg 72.32) while request_rate is ~0.4 req/s; memory_pct is flat/unremarkable at ~49-51% throughout (no growth or OOM trend).

error_rate (HTTP 5xx % of requests) stays flat at ~0.2% across the entire window including onset (0.17-0.26), i.e. the failure is not surfacing as HTTP 5xx — consistent with a consumer-side blocking stall rather than request-serving failure.

Onset order is tight: metric bucket 07:40-07:45 already shows lag rising (avg 515.03) and request_rate decaying (avg 25.87, max 65.3 = partial bucket), while the first explicit ERROR is 07:42:14Z. The 5-min bucket boundary means the true inflection is between 07:40 and 07:42; the matched error timestamp 07:42:14Z is the sharpest available onset marker.

Exactly one deployment falls in the onset window anywhere in the fleet: dep-6010 order-service v2.16.0 at 2026-05-12T07:40:00Z (author a.khan, 'Order events v2'), changes 'OrderExecuted event: rename field qty -> quantity', 'add field venue', 'event schema version header v2', status live, rolled_back_at null. Deployed 2 min 14 s before the first settlement-service deserialize error at 07:42:14Z on orders-3@8841207 ('missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)'). This is the only change that directly matches the observed error signature.

Exactly one config change exists in the whole window: cfg-3004 on settlement-service, key 'consumer.max.poll.records' reduced 500 -> 200 at 2026-05-12T07:35:00Z by m.das ('Smaller poll batches to smooth DB writes'). No rollback recorded. It touches the consumer poll path but changes only batch SIZE, not deserialization/schema handling, and precedes the onset by 7 min 14 s.

Ruled out as sole cause: the poll-settings change (cfg-3004) would throttle consumption rate but cannot produce a per-message deserialize failure or a poison-message retry loop on a single fixed offset; smaller poll batches (500->200, still 200 records) would not drive request_rate to a sustained ~0.4 req/s floor. Evidence: T1's first error at 07:42:14Z is a schema mismatch on orders-3@8841207 ('missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)') and 'partition blocked' retry at 07:44:51Z attempt 92490 — symptoms tied to message CONTENT, not to poll batch size. Its temporal proximity (7 min before onset) makes it a candidate only in combination, not as the mechanism.

findings.statement: Downstream-dependency change ruled out: settlement-service has only two edges, 'queue-consume -> kafka' and 'db -> ledger-db'; no deployment or config change was recorded for kafka, ledger-db, or any other platform component in 06:00-09:59, and no deployment at all in the window except dep-6010 (order-service). ledger-db is a shared postgres and kafka is shared, so a third party COULD affect settlement-service, but no change event documents such an action in this window — the DB/broker path shows no correlated change.

Upstream producer change is the best-fitting candidate: order-service (the OrderExecuted producer) was the only service to deploy in the window (dep-6010, 07:40:00Z), its change explicitly renames the OrderExecuted field 'qty -> quantity' and sets 'event schema version header v2', which is exactly the mismatch settlement-service reports ('missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)'). A producer emitting v2 messages that a v1 consumer cannot deserialize directly explains a poison message stalling a partition and monotonic lag growth, while a poll-size reduction cannot.

Historical precedents found are all Kafka partition-assignment/rebalance events (HIST-112 settlement-service 'Consumer lost partition assignment during broker maintenance'; HIST-104 'Partition reassignment caused consumer group rebalancing storm'), both infrastructure_failure. These match the symptom ('consumer lag growing', 'settlements stuck') but NOT the current error signature (poison message / schema mismatch), and no rebalance/config change is documented here — leads only, not evidence.

refs.quote: Consumer lost partition assignment during broker maintenance

findings.statement: The 'orders' topic (the kafka component) has exactly FOUR producer/consumer edges: two producers - order-service and payment-service, both 'queue-produce -> kafka' - and two consumers - settlement-service and notification-service, both 'queue-consume -> kafka'. No other service in the fleet has a produce or consume edge to kafka.

order-service's dependency graph contains only ONE publish edge: 'order-service -> kafka kind queue-produce'. Its other outbound edges are db to ledger-db, http to pricing-engine and http to exchange-gateway - so kafka is order-service's sole event-emission channel and any OrderExecuted v2 event it emits must traverse this single producer edge.

The second producer on kafka, payment-service, is also connected to kafka and ledger-db, but is NOT the source of the OrderExecuted v2 schema change: it has 0 deployments in the window 2026-05-11T00:00Z - 2026-05-12T09:59Z and no matching change record, while the OrderExecuted v2 change is attributed to dep-6010 order-service.

dep-6010 order-service v2.16.0 (deployed 2026-05-12T07:40:00Z, author a.khan, 'Order events v2', status live, rolled_back_at null) is the ONLY deployment on order-service in the entire window 2026-05-11T00:00Z - 2026-05-12T09:59Z, and order-service records exactly 0 config changes in that window - so this deployment is the only order-service-originating change that could have altered its emitted OrderExecuted payload/partition routing.

No producer-config, routing or producer->topic-partition mapping record is retrievable for dep-6010 or order-service: order-service has 0 config changes in the window and the deployment record contains only the three summary change strings ('rename qty -> quantity', 'add field venue', 'event schema version header v2') with no topic or partition assignment. Therefore the specific topic/partition that order-service's OrderExecuted v2 writes to is not documented in available data.

findings.statement: The only config change anywhere in 06:00-09:59 on 2026-05-12 is cfg-3004 on settlement-service (consumer.max.poll.records 500->200, 07:35:00Z); no kafka/broker-side config change, rebalance trigger or partition-reassignment event is recorded, so nothing in the change data shows a third party perturbing partition orders-3 on the broker.

The only ERROR-log signature on the orders consumer path in this task's data is settlement-service's: 409 ERROR entries, 100% on partition orders-3 at offset 8841207, matching 'failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)'. The same signature appears repeatedly (e.g. 07:42:14Z, 07:42:23Z, 07:42:51Z, 07:43:22Z, 07:43:55Z ...) through 09:58:31Z. No other partition id appears in any of the 40 returned entries.

findings.statement: Searches for settlement-service log text indicating a rebalance or a partition-assignment change in/around 07:40-07:45Z returned ZERO matches in the window 07:35-09:59Z ('rebalance' → total_matched 0; 'assigned' → total_matched 0), i.e. no rebalance/assignment event is recorded on settlement-service in this window in the log data available.

notification-service (another known service on the platform) shows NO deserialize failures in 07:30-09:59Z: a query for 'deserialize' at WARN+ returned total_matched 0. This is a hard negative for one other service but is not evidence about whether notification-service consumes the 'orders' topic.

Confirmed independently that settlement-service's consumer_lag is monotonic and starts climbing exactly at the 07:40 bucket: 06:30-07:32 baseline stays in the 35-64 range (07:32 bucket avg 48.31, max 54.61), then 07:40 bucket avg 1137.31 / max 2544.42, rising every bucket to avg 60412.45 / max 61605.53. The metric is a group-level aggregate; the data retrieved does not break it down per partition, so it cannot by itself show whether only orders-3 or all assigned partitions contribute.

The order-service's own logs do NOT corroborate a producer-side error: a query of order-service for WARN+ entries containing 'qty' in 07:35-09:59Z returned total_matched 0, so order-service logged no error about the renamed field anywhere in the window. (Its log data_range is 04:00-09:59Z, so the window is covered.)

settlement-service exposes NO partition-dimensioned lag/commit metric: its available_metrics list is exactly [consumer_lag, cpu_pct, db_pool_in_use, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts]. A query for a candidate per-partition metric 'consumer_lag_partition' returned not_found with the same 8-metric list, confirming no partition dimension is offered.

The finest available lag granularity for the settlement consumer group is the group-level aggregate 'consumer_lag', downsampled to bucket_seconds=1080 (18-minute buckets). Over 06:30-09:48Z it shows a clean monotonic climb: baseline 40.82-45.87 avg (06:30-07:24), then 4164.42 avg at 07:42, rising to 58846.66 avg / 61605.53 max at 09:48. This aggregate cannot separate orders-3 from other assigned partitions.

The kafka component similarly exposes no per-partition or per-consumer-group lag metric: its available_metrics are only [cpu_pct, messages_in_per_s, under_replicated_partitions], and 'consumer_lag' is not_found for it. So no broker-side series can be used to break lag down by partition either.

Because neither settlement-service nor kafka exposes a partition dimension, the question of whether lag growth is confined to orders-3 or spread across all assigned partitions CANNOT be answered from metric telemetry. The only partition-level signal available is message content/tags in logs (orders-3@8841207), not a lag/commit series; the aggregate metric is consistent with either a single blocked partition or fleet-wide lag.
